results.content:
President Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to yet another low since his return to the White House, according to a new Economist/YouGov poll, which also found that just 1 in 3 Americans approve of his job performance.

The survey, released Aug. 11, found that 33% of Americans approve of Trump's performance, down 3 percentage points from the previous week. This marks the lowest approval rating the president has seen in YouGov tracking since he returned to office in 2025. [...] Advertisement

The latest poll also found that Trump's age continues to concern the American public, with 53% saying they believed the 80-year-old president was too old to be in the White House.

As for the Senate, Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win a majority in that chamber. Despite the aforementioned trends in the Democrats' favor, that will be difficult. They will need to retain all seats they currently hold, including those for Georgia and Michigan, states that Trump captured in 2024, and "flip" four of five seats—in Alaska, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, and Texas—where the Republican candidates are vulnerable.
